abstract.para: Btrfs is a copy-on-write (CoW) file system for Linux. When the content of a file changes, Btrfs does not overwrite the existing blocks. Instead, it writes the modified data to new blocks and then links the change into the file system metadata. Until the last write finishes, Btrfs does not commit the new changes.

topic.para: This behavior is the foundation of subvolumes and snapshots. Unchanged data is never copied, so Btrfs can capture the state of a file system at a point in time quickly and with minimal disk space usage. The same mechanism allows copying single files without duplicating their data. For example, the command cp --reflink=always creates a copy that shares its blocks with the original file until one of them changes.

section.title: Key features of Btrfs
section.para: Btrfs provides fault tolerance, repair and management features. The following features are relevant for subvolumes and snapshots:

listitem.para: Writable snapshots for rolling back a system after updates or for backing up files
Subvolumes that act as individual file systems within the same pool of space
Online check and repair of data and metadata with the btrfs scrub command
Different RAID profiles and different checksums for metadata and user data
Offline migration from existing Ext2, Ext3 and Ext4 file systems
Boot loader support for booting from a Btrfs partition

section.para: The number of subvolumes is limited only by the space allocated to the pool. For the RAID profiles that SUSE supports, see the documentation of your product.
